blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At executive level, the software portfolio is architecture, not a purchase history. Every tool the company runs — ERP, CRM, HR, finance, analytics — is a strategic bet. Taken together, they form a structure that either supports the business the company is trying to become or quietly constrains it.

The senior leader's task is to keep the portfolio coherent. Every serious software decision should answer two questions: does this tool fit the architecture we are building, and what does it mean for the tools we already have? A company whose answer to both questions drifts over five years ends up with dozens of tools that were each chosen well in isolation and together make no sense at all.

Coherence costs something. It means refusing some attractive new tools because they do not fit. It means slowing down integration decisions by a few weeks. It means, occasionally, retiring something loved because it no longer belongs. All of this is worth it — because software architecture, once tangled, is very expensive to untangle.

items.q: According to the text, at executive level the software portfolio should be understood as…
options: a purchase history
an IT cost centre
a list of vendors
an architecture
items.why: "the software portfolio is architecture, not a purchase history" — a tese central da lição.

items.q: What two questions should every serious software decision answer?
options: How cheap it is and how quickly it can be deployed
Whether competitors use it and whether staff already know it
Whether it fits the architecture and what it means for existing tools
Who owns the budget and who signs the contract
items.why: "does this tool fit the architecture we are building, and what does it mean for the tools we already have?"

items.q: The phrase "each chosen well in isolation and together make no sense at all" suggests that…
options: isolation is the best way to evaluate software
individually sound choices can still produce an incoherent whole
the tools were all poor choices from the start
coherence is impossible in large companies
items.why: Inferência: cada compra pode ser boa sozinha e, somadas sem coerência, o conjunto perde sentido.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A portfolio can quietly constrain the business it should support.
Coherence is worth a few weeks of delay.
Any tool that looks attractive should be adopted quickly.
Retiring a valued tool can be the right decision.
items.why: Inferência: o texto defende recusar ferramentas atraentes que não encaixam — o oposto de adotar depressa o que parece bom.

items.q: Why does the author stress that architecture is "very expensive to untangle"?
options: To recommend buying only from one vendor
To justify paying the cost of coherence upfront
To show that integration is always impossible
To argue that software should never be changed
items.why: Inferência: o custo alto de desemaranhar depois é o que torna a coerência antecipada válida — "All of this is worth it".

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry defendendo sua posição numa reunião de arquitetura de software. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
I know I'm the only voice in this room saying no to the tool, and I know how that looks. Everyone in that demo wanted it, and honestly, on its own merits, it's an excellent product.

But that's exactly the trap. We don't evaluate tools on their own merits any more — we evaluate them against the architecture we're trying to build. And this one doesn't fit it. It duplicates two things we already run, it holds its own copy of customer data, and it won't integrate cleanly with the platform we chose as our backbone last year.

So yes, we could buy it this quarter and everyone leaves happy. But in three years we'd be paying someone to untangle it from everything else, and by then the mess is baked in. Coherence is boring. It means occasionally being the person who slows things down. I'd rather be that person now than apologise for a tangled estate later.

Give me two weeks. Let me map how it would actually sit inside what we have. If I'm wrong, I'll be the first to sign off on it.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Harry describe the tool the room wants to buy?
options: An excellent product on its own merits
A tool nobody in the demo liked
An overpriced and weak product
A tool identical to their current backbone
items.why: "on its own merits, it's an excellent product" — ele não nega a qualidade da ferramenta.

items.q: What are the specific reasons Harry gives for the tool not fitting?
options: It is disliked by the customer-facing teams
It is too expensive and hard to license
It is untested and lacks support
It duplicates existing tools, holds its own customer data, and won't integrate cleanly
items.why: "It duplicates two things we already run, it holds its own copy of customer data, and it won't integrate cleanly."

items.q: What does Harry mean by "the mess is baked in"?
options: The tool will stop working after three years
The data will be permanently deleted
The problem becomes fixed and hard to reverse over time
The budget will be spent before delivery
items.why: Inferência: "baked in" = entranhado; depois de três anos o emaranhado fica difícil de desfazer.

items.q: What does Harry's offer to "map how it would actually sit inside what we have" reveal about his position?
options: He has already decided nothing will ever change
He is only defending his personal preference
He wants to delay every decision indefinitely
He is open to being proven wrong by evidence
items.why: Inferência: "If I'm wrong, I'll be the first to sign off on it" — a recusa é condicional, baseada em análise.

items.q: How would you best describe Harry's tone?
options: Principled but self-aware about being unpopular
Indifferent to the outcome
Uncertain and easily persuaded
Aggressive and dismissive of his colleagues
items.why: Inferência: ele reconhece que ninguém o agradece hoje ("I'd rather be that person now"), mas mantém o argumento — firme e autoconsciente.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Treat the portfolio as strategic architecture, not a shopping list." Here architecture means…
options: the deliberate overall structure of how the parts fit together
the software licensing agreement
the IT department's headcount
the design of the office building
items.why: Architecture = arquitetura: a estrutura intencional que organiza como as peças se encaixam.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Each tool is a strategic bet, so we should ask what future it commits us to." A strategic bet is…
options: a wager on which the company's future partly depends
a temporary trial with no consequences
a discount negotiated with a vendor
a routine administrative purchase
items.why: Strategic bet = aposta estratégica: uma escolha da qual o futuro da empresa depende em parte.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "If our answers ___ over five years, the portfolio loses its coherence."
options: drift
untangle
integrate
retire
items.why: To drift = desviar aos poucos; é o que corrói a coerência ao longo do tempo.

items.q: "Each tool was chosen well in isolation." This phrase means the tools were judged…
options: under time pressure
against the competitors' choices
by a single decision-maker
separately, without reference to the whole
items.why: In isolation = isoladamente: avaliadas uma a uma, sem olhar o conjunto.

items.q: "Once the estate is tangled, it is very expensive to untangle." Tangled here describes a system that is…
options: so interconnected and messy that it is hard to separate
newly installed and untested
fully documented and clearly mapped
cheap and easy to replace
items.why: Tangled = emaranhado: tão interligado e confuso que se torna difícil de desemaranhar (untangle).

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre arquitetura de software. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The architecture board still has to sign off on the new tool." To sign off on means to…
options: formally approve
quietly ignore
comment informally
announce publicly
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "Harry decided to push back on the popular new tool." He…
options: resisted or challenged the proposal
rewrote the vendor's contract
postponed reading the demo notes
approved it without discussion
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "We'll phase out the legacy tool once the new backbone is stable." To phase out means to…
options: buy more licences for it
integrate it with everything else
restore it to full service
gradually withdraw it from use
items.why: Phase out = desativar aos poucos, retirar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Adopting that tool now would lock us into a vendor for a decade." This means it would…
options: guarantee the tool never changes price
give us full freedom to switch later
reduce our long-term costs automatically
commit us in a way that is hard to escape
items.why: Lock (someone) into = prender numa escolha difícil de reverter — o custo de saída fica alto.

items.q: "Buying it in isolation would store up problems for later." To store up problems means to…
options: document risks carefully
share the workload with another team
create trouble that surfaces in the future
solve issues in advance
items.why: Store up (trouble/problems) = acumular problemas que só aparecem mais tarde.
